blocks.task_summary: Find the number of ways to place 5 sheep in 6 pens (each pen holds all sheep) such that Amber and Brownie are not in the same pen.
method_path: Place Brownie in a different pen: 5 choices
Place each of Curly, Daisy, Eden: 6 choices each
accepted_alternatives: Total placements without restriction: 6⁵ = 7776. Placements with Amber and Brownie together: choose 1 of 6 pens for both, then 6 choices each for remaining 3 sheep → 6 × 6³ = 6⁴ = 1296. Subtract: 7776 − 1296 = 6480.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: B has one less pen to select (M1), A and B can be placed in 6×5 ways (A1), C, D, E have 6 choices each (A1), 5×6⁴ = 6480 (A1). METHOD 2: total number of ways 6⁵ (A1), number of ways with Amber and Brownie together 6⁴ (A1), attempt to subtract (M1), 6⁵−6⁴ = 5×6⁴ = 6480 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find the number of ways to place 5 sheep in 6 pens (one sheep per pen) such that Amber and Brownie are not in boundary-sharing pens in the 3×2 grid.
method_path: Count boundary-sharing adjacent pairs in 3×2 grid: 7 pairs
Arrangements with Amber and Brownie sharing a boundary: 2 × 7 × 4! = 336
accepted_alternatives: Case analysis by pen type: A in corner (4 corners) → B has 3 safe pens, remaining 4 sheep in 4! ways → 4 × 3 × 4! = 288. A in middle pen (2 pens) → B has 2 safe pens, remaining 4 sheep in 4! ways → 2 × 2 × 4! = 96. Total: 288 + 96 = 384.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: total number of ways 6! = 720 (A1), number of ways with Amber and Brownie sharing a boundary = 2×7×4! = 336 (A1), attempt to subtract (M1), 720−336 = 384 (A1). METHOD 2: case 1 placing A in corner pen: 4×(3×4×3×2×1) = 12×4! = 288 (A1), case 2 placing A in middle pen: 2×(2×4×3×2×1) = 4×4! = 96 (A1), attempt to add (M1), 288+96 = 384 (A1).
